Sk.</ls> .²4 Drift, tenor, purport. .²5 Race, family, lineage; रघूणामन्वयं वक्षये <ls>R. 1. 9</ls>, <ls n="R. 1.">12</ls>, <ls n="R.">3. 27</ls>, <ls n="R.">12. 33</ls>; अन्वयगुणः <ls>Mv. 4. 22</ls> virtue of my race. .²6 Descendants, posterity; ताभ्य ऋते अन्वयः <ls>Y. 2. 117</ls>; स˚ along with the family or descendants; <ls>Ms. 2. 168</ls>; जातस्तु गण्यते सोऽत्र यः स्फुरत्यन्वयाधिकम् <ls>Pt. 1. 27</ls>. .²7 Logical connection of cause and effect, logical continuance; जन्माद्यस्य यतोऽन्वयादितरतः <ls>Bhāg. 1. 1. 1</ls>. .²8 Being seen (प्रत्यक्ष); स्यात्साहसं त्वन्वयवत् प्रसभं कर्म यत्कृतम् . निरन्वयं भवेत्स्तेयम् … <ls>Ms. 8. 332</ls>. .²9 (In Nyāya) Statement of the constant and invariable concomitance of the हेतु (middle term) and the साध्य (major term) of an Indian syllogism (हेतुसाध्ययोर्व्याप्तिरन्वयः). In the familiar instance पर्वतो वह्निमान् धूमवत्त्वात् the relation यत्र यत्र धूमस्तत्र तत्र वह्निः (wherever there is smoke there is fire) is called अन्वय or अन्वयव्याप्ति. अन्वय, in fact, corresponds to the universal proposition of European logic ‘All A is B’. The ‘व्यतिरेकव्याप्ति’ means an assertion of the concomitance of the absence of साध्य and the absence of हेतु (तदभावयोः हेत्वभावसाध्याभावयोः व्याप्तिः) and corresponds to the converted A proposition ‘All not-B is not-A’; or in Sanskrit यत्र यत्र वह्निर्नास्ति तत्र तत्र धूमोऽपि नास्ति; and a cause or हेतु is said to be connected with its effect by अन्वयव्यतिरेकव्याप्ति when both the affirmative and negative relations between the thing to be proved and the cause that proves can be equally asserted; such a {%Hetu%} alone makes the argument perfectly sound and incapable of refutation. This process of arriving at the Vyāpti or universal proposition corresponds to the methods of Agreement and Difference in Millʼs Logic; साध्ये निश्चितमन्वयेन घटितम् <ls>Mu. 5. 10</ls>.
